Editorial, authoritative, says "we've been here for years."
- **Text font:** **Jost** (Google Fonts). A clean geometric sans-serif — the kind used on modern packaging labels. Think "flour bag, not software."

|---|---|---|

**Fraunces is the decision.** It's the only display font across these three directions that has personality baked into the letterform itself — you don't have to work to make it feel warm, it just does. # ARCHITECTURE.md — TruckLine

---

## 1. Stack Decision

> **Terms explained on first use:** *Edge Function* = a small piece of server code that runs on demand in the cloud, not on your computer. *RLS* = Row-Level Security, database rules that decide who can read or write each row. *JWT* = JSON Web Token, a tamper-proof digital pass signed by the server and carried by the browser. *Anon key* = a public Supabase key that only works within the bounds of RLS rules. *Service role key* = a Supabase key that bypasses all rules — must never leave the server.

| Layer | Choice | Why | Rejected Alternative & Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Frontend** | React — *Lovable decides this* | Lovable generates React; don't fight it | — |
| **Backend / API** | Supabase Edge Functions (Deno / TypeScript) | Lovable's native backend layer; serverless, zero infrastructure | Firebase Functions — not Lovable-native, adds a separate Google account and setup |
| **Database** | Supabase PostgreSQL + RLS | Bundled with Lovable/Supabase; relational rows fit the entities perfectly; RLS enforces access rules at the database level | PlanetScale / Neon — not Lovable-native; extra accounts for no gain |
| **Auth** | Supabase Auth (Owner) + custom PIN → server-signed JWT (Helper) + no auth / UUID token (Customer) | Each role needs a different trust model; Supabase Auth handles Owner; PIN avoids creating email accounts for helpers; customers have no accounts at all | Clerk / Auth0 — extra service, extra cost, not Lovable-native |
| **File storage** | None in V1 | Spec has no images or uploads | Supabase Storage — available for V2 if menu photos are added |
| **Payments** | Square Hosted Checkout | Spec requires it; customer leaves your page to pay on Square's page, so you never touch card data (no PCI scope) | Stripe — spec explicitly names Square |
| **AI / LLM** | None | Not in spec | — |
| **Hosting** | Lovable (frontend) + Supabase (Edge Functions + DB) | Both free tiers; Lovable deploys your React app automatically | Vercel / Netlify — viable but an extra account Lovable already replaces |
| **SMS / Notifications** | Twilio | Most reliable; sends texts via a simple API call from an Edge Function; ~$0.008 per SMS | **No truly free production SMS service exists.** Resend (email, free 3,000/month) is the $0 fallback if you must avoid Twilio costs, but the spec says SMS. |

---

## 2. System Diagram

    H([Helper Browser])
    O([Owner Browser])
    FE[React App\nLovable Hosting\n— untrusted —]

    end

**Risk 1 — Slot double-booking race condition**
Two customers grab the last slot at exactly the same moment.

**Risk 2 — Square webhook never fires**
A customer pays successfully on Square's page, but Square's notification to your server gets lost, leaving the order stuck in `pending_payment` forever.

A customer holds a slot and abandons the tab. The 5-minute hold lingers if no cleanup runs.

Sending unsolicited text messages in the US without written consent is a federal violation with fines up to $1,500 per message.
*Mitigation:* Show an explicit opt-in checkbox at checkout: *"Text me when my order is ready (message and data rates may apply)."* Store `sms_consent = true` and `consent_at` timestamp in the Order record. - **Your app has two separate computers doing work.** The one running in the customer's browser handles only what they see — menus, forms, and buttons. # SPEC.md — What the App Does Today

## One-liner
A private massage studio booking site where clients discover services, pay via Stripe, upload health intake forms, and message the studio owner — all behind Supabase authentication.

---

## Users & Roles

| Role | What they can do today | **Must NEVER do** |
|---|---|---|
| **Unauthenticated visitor** | Browse the service list (prices are public) | Access any user's bookings, messages, or files |
| **Client** (authenticated, role = `'client'`) | Book & pay for a service; view their own bookings; upload/view their own files; send and receive messages | See another client's bookings, messages, or files; set their own role; decide their own payment status; message another client directly |
| **Staff** (authenticated, role = `'staff'`) | Exactly the same as a client — no extra database policies exist | Access data that belongs to clients they are not in conversation with; change booking statuses |
| **Admin** (authenticated, role = `'admin'`) | Exactly the same as a client — no extra database policies exist | Be unable to see all bookings, all messages, and all uploaded files (this is a current bug — admin *cannot* do what they should) |
| **Stripe webhook** (server, uses service-role key) | Write a confirmed `bookings` row | Write to any table other than bookings via this route |

> **Plain English — "Row Level Security" (RLS):** RLS means the database itself checks who is asking before handing over any data. Even if someone steals a user's login token, they can only see that one user's rows, not everyone else's.

---

## Core Loop

```
Visitor lands → (login/signup) → picks a service → clicks "Book and pay"
→ server creates a Stripe checkout page → Stripe processes card
→ Stripe sends a signed receipt (webhook) to the server
→ server marks the booking "paid" in the database
→ client uploads intake form → sends message to studio
→ admin reviews (currently has no UI to do so — see Edge Cases)
```

| Layer | Technology | Plain-English meaning |

| Frontend | React (built with Vite) | The part you see in the browser; a JavaScript app |

> **Plain English — "JWT":** A JSON Web Token is a signed digital ticket that proves who you are. Supabase issues one when you log in; your browser sends it with every request so the server knows it's really you.
>
> **Plain English — "service-role key":** A master key that bypasses all security rules. Only the webhook function holds it; it never touches the browser.
>
> **Plain English — "HMAC signature":** Stripe signs every webhook with a secret only you and Stripe know. Your server checks this signature before trusting the event — otherwise anyone could fake a "payment confirmed" message.

## Known Risks (as built today)

1. **No elevated RLS for admin/staff** — admin cannot manage the business through the app.
2. **Browser-only file validation** — storage accepts any file type from an authenticated user in their folder.
3. **Free-text `sender_name`** — trivial identity spoofing in the message list.
4. **No webhook for refunds** — financial records go stale after a dispute.
5. **No role assigned on signup** — new users exist in auth but not in `user_roles`.
6. **Single migration file** — no forward-only migration strategy; changes to the schema will be hard to manage safely.
7. **Hardcoded URLs** in checkout function (`https://cleanbook.app/done`) — breaks silently if domain changes.

## In Plain English (5 bullets)

- **Your Stripe secret and database admin key never touch the browser** — they only live on Supabase's servers inside the two Edge Functions. This is the most important security thing the app gets right.
- **The database is the real security layer** — even if someone tricks the browser code, Supabase's Row Level Security rules stop them from reading data that isn't theirs.
- **Stripe, not your app, handles the card** — your server only gets a "payment done" notification after the fact, and it verifies that message is genuinely from Stripe before trusting it.
- **The price is always fetched from your database** — a client cannot fiddle with the browser to change what they pay; the server ignores any price the browser might send.
- **Right now, your admin login can't do more than a regular client login** — there are no database rules granting admin or staff extra visibility, which means you currently can't manage your own business through the app.

# GAP LIST — Ranked by Risk

> **How to read this list:** Each item names the risk in plain English, gives a severity rating, and says exactly where in the code it lives.

## 🔴 CRITICAL

### GAP-01 · Health data stored with no Business Associate Agreement confirmed
**Risk:** Intake forms uploaded by clients almost certainly contain Protected Health Information (medications, injuries, medical history). Storing this data with Supabase (and routing metadata through Stripe) without a signed BAA may violate HIPAA. This is not legal advice — consult a healthcare privacy attorney before acquiring more users.
**Where:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` (storage bucket `client-files`), `src/pages/Files.jsx`

---

### GAP-02 · Admin and staff cannot see any client data through the app
**Risk:** The app is live and taking real payments, but the admin cannot view other users' bookings, messages, or uploaded files — the same RLS policies that protect clients also block admin. The studio cannot be managed through the app. This is both an operational failure and a safety issue (admin cannot review intake forms before a session).
**Where:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — no admin-elevated policies on `bookings`, `messages`, or `storage.objects`; no admin dashboard in any provided file

---

### GAP-03 · File type and size validation exists only in the browser
**Risk:** A technically savvy user can bypass `Files.jsx`'s type/size check entirely (e.g., using `curl` or browser dev tools) and upload any file — executable code, HTML, or multi-gigabyte files — directly to your Supabase Storage bucket. The storage RLS policy allows any file from a user's own folder.
**Where:** `src/pages/Files.jsx` lines 3–4 (browser check); `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` storage INSERT policy (no MIME or size restriction)

---

## 🟠 HIGH

### GAP-04 · `sender_name` is a free-text field — any user can impersonate anyone
**Risk:** A client can set `sender_name` to "Studio Owner" or "Admin" when sending a message. The Messages component displays the name exactly as stored, with no verification against the actual user account. This enables social engineering attacks against other clients or staff.
**Where:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — no check constraint or server-side override on `messages.sender_name`; `src/pages/Messages.jsx` renders it directly

---

### GAP-05 · A client can send a message directly to another client
**Violates "must NEVER" rule:** Clients must never be able to message each other.
**Risk:** The insert policy on `messages` only checks `auth.uid() = from_id`. It places no restriction on `to_id`. Any client who knows (or guesses) another client's UUID can send them a direct message, and both parties can read that thread via the SELECT policy.
**Where:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — `"send as yourself"` policy, line `with check (auth.uid() = from_id)`

---

### GAP-06 · No role is assigned when a new user signs up
**Risk:** Every new user has a row in `auth.users` but no row in `user_roles`. Any code that reads `user_roles` for that user gets `null`. If role-gating logic is added later, new users will be silently blocked or silently given no restrictions depending on how the check is written. The current code never checks the role table before granting access.
**Where:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — no `AFTER INSERT ON auth.users` trigger or default role insertion

---

### GAP-07 · No Stripe refund, cancellation, or dispute webhook
**Risk:** When a client disputes or is refunded a charge, Stripe fires `charge.refunded` and `payment_intent.payment_failed` events. The webhook handler ignores all event types except `checkout.session.completed`. The booking stays `status = 'paid'` permanently, creating a false financial record and a possible situation where a refunded client still appears as a confirmed booking.
**Where:** `supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts` — only `checkout.session.completed` handled

---

### GAP-08 · Booking confirmation page shown before webhook has fired
**Risk:** After Stripe checkout the client is redirected to `https://cleanbook.app/done`. At that moment the webhook has not necessarily been processed. If the `/done` page queries the database to show booking details, it will find nothing. Worse, the client may think the booking failed and try to pay again.
**Where:** `supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts` — `success_url: 'https://cleanbook.app/done'`

---

## 🟡 MEDIUM

### GAP-09 · No server-side MIME type enforcement in storage bucket policies
**Risk:** Even if browser validation were fixed, the Supabase storage INSERT policy does not filter by content type. A server-side approach (storage policy condition on `storage.mimetype`) or a post-upload scan is needed to reliably enforce file types.
**Where:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — `"own folder write"` storage policy

---

### GAP-10 · No rate limiting on messages
**Risk:** An authenticated client can insert messages in a tight loop, filling the `messages` table and flooding any notification channel the studio owner uses.
**Where:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — `"send as yourself"` policy; no throttle mechanism

---

### GAP-11 · No rate limiting on the checkout Edge Function
**Risk:** An authenticated user can call the `checkout` function in rapid succession, creating dozens of open Stripe sessions. Stripe charges per session at some tiers and this could also be used for denial-of-service against your Stripe account.
**Where:** `supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts` — no rate-limit check before `stripe.checkout.sessions.create`

**Risk:** If a future code path or direct database access ever writes an unrecognized status string, the booking record will be silently corrupted. Adding `check (status in ('pending','paid','refunded','cancelled'))` costs nothing and prevents it.

**Risk:** The `services` table has a public read policy but no write policy for any role. Creating a new service, changing a price, or removing a service requires direct database access (Supabase dashboard or service-role API call). If the studio's prices change, there is no UI to update them.

**Risk:** The `user_roles` table has a `'staff'` value but zero RLS policies reference it. Assigning staff to someone gives them no additional capability over a regular client. Any feature built for staff in the future must include corresponding policies, or staff will still be blocked.

## Glossary of Terms Used
- **Row Level Security (RLS)**: Database rules attached to each table that automatically filter which rows a user can read or write, based on their identity.
- **JWT (JSON Web Token)**: A digitally signed "pass" that proves who you are. Supabase issues one when you log in; you send it with every request.
- **Edge Function**: A small server program (here written in Deno/TypeScript) that runs on Supabase's infrastructure — not on your own servers.
- **Service Role Key**: A master key that bypasses all RLS rules entirely. Whoever holds it can read and write anything in the database.
- **Anon Key**: A public identifier for your Supabase project. Safe to expose in the browser *only if* every table has RLS correctly configured.
- **Webhook**: An automatic HTTP POST message that Stripe sends to your server the moment a payment event occurs (e.g., payment succeeded).
- **HMAC signature**: A cryptographic stamp Stripe adds to each webhook so your server can prove the message really came from Stripe and wasn't tampered with.

*Each entry lists: Severity, a plain-English description of the risk, and exactly where in the code it lives.*

---

### 🔴 CRITICAL

---

**GAP-01 — Health data stored with no confirmed data-protection agreement**
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Risk:** Intake forms (uploaded files) almost certainly contain Protected Health Information. If HIPAA applies and there is no BAA with Supabase, the operator may be in violation of federal law every day the app is live.
- **Location:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` (bucket creation: `'client-files'`); `src/pages/Files.jsx` (upload function)

---

**GAP-02 — Staff and Admin roles exist in the database but are not enforced anywhere**
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Risk:** The `user_roles` table defines `staff` and `admin`, but no RLS policy on any other table checks those roles. This means: (a) admin/staff cannot see all bookings, messages, or files through the normal app — the admin dashboard is either broken or, far worse, has been built using the service role key in the browser (which would be a master key in the hands of anyone who can read page source).
- **Location:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — the `user_roles` table has a read-own-row policy but no policy on `bookings`, `messages`, or `client-files` references `user_roles`

---

### 🟠 HIGH

---

**GAP-03 — `sender_name` in messages is free text controlled entirely by the sender**
- **Severity:** High
- **Risk:** Any client can insert a message with `sender_name = 'Studio Admin'` or `sender_name = 'Staff'`. Because the read policy only checks `from_id` / `to_id` and not `sender_name`, the recipient (including admin) will see a convincingly labeled fake message. In a health context, this could be used to give false medical guidance appearing to come from the studio.
- **Location:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — `messages` insert policy only checks `auth.uid() = from_id`; `src/pages/Messages.jsx` — renders `m.sender_name` directly from the DB

---

**GAP-04 — No webhook handlers for refunds, disputes, or session expiry**
- **Severity:** High
- **Risk:** If a client is refunded or files a chargeback, `bookings.status` remains `'paid'` permanently. The studio has no way to know the payment was reversed from within the app, and the client retains any access tied to "paid" status.
- **Location:** `supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts` — only handles `checkout.session.completed`; no handler for `charge.dispute.created`, `charge.refunded`, `checkout.session.expired`

---

**GAP-05 — Admin and staff cannot read client intake files**
- **Severity:** High
- **Risk:** The entire point of intake forms is for the therapist to review them before a session. No storage policy exists granting admin or staff access to the `client-files` bucket. This makes the file upload feature non-functional for its business purpose.
- **Location:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — storage policies `"own folder read"` and `"own folder write"` restrict access to the folder owner only

---

**GAP-06 — Book button has no loading/disabled state — multiple Stripe sessions can be created**
- **Severity:** High
- **Risk:** A user who clicks "Book and pay" multiple times before the async call completes will create multiple Stripe Checkout sessions. If they complete more than one, they will be charged multiple times for the same service, and multiple booking records will be created.
- **Location:** `src/pages/Book.jsx` — `pay()` function has no guard; no `disabled` attribute on the button

---

### 🟡 MEDIUM

---

**GAP-07 — Client can send a message to any other valid user, including other clients**
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Risk:** The `messages` insert policy only requires `from_id = auth.uid()`. There is no constraint on `to_id`. A client who knows another client's user ID could message them directly, violating privacy expectations.
- **Location:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — `"send as yourself"` policy: `with check (auth.uid() = from_id)` with no `to_id` restriction

---

**GAP-08 — File type and size validation is browser-only**
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Risk:** The `ALLOWED` type check and 5 MB limit in `Files.jsx` runs only in the browser. A developer tool or scripted request can bypass it and upload arbitrary file types or larger files directly to the Supabase Storage API.
- **Location:** `src/pages/Files.jsx` — `if (!ALLOWED.includes(file.type) || file.size > 5_000_000)` is client-side only; no MIME-type restriction is set in the storage bucket policy in `001_init.sql`

---

**GAP-09 — No rate limiting on messages or file uploads**
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Risk:** Any authenticated user can send unlimited messages or upload unlimited files. A malicious or malfunctioning client could flood the studio's inbox or exhaust storage quotas, making the app unusable.
- **Location:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — no rate-limit policy or row count constraint on `messages`; `src/pages/Files.jsx` — no upload frequency guard

---

**GAP-10 — No `created_at` timestamp on the `bookings` table**
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Risk:** There is no record of when a booking was made. The studio cannot sort upcoming appointments, detect same-day double-bookings, or produce a basic schedule view.
- **Location:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — `bookings` table definition lacks `created_at`

---

**GAP-11 — `success_url` and `cancel_url` are hardcoded strings in the edge function**
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Risk:** If the domain changes or a staging environment is used, the edge function must be manually edited to avoid redirecting users to the wrong URL. There is also no way to pass per-booking context (e.g., which service was booked) back to the success page.
- **Location:** `supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts` — `success_url: 'https://cleanbook.app/done'`, `cancel_url: 'https://cleanbook.app/book'`

---

**GAP-12 — No new-user onboarding creates a default `user_roles` row**
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Risk:** Nothing in the provided code inserts a row into `user_roles` when a new user registers. If the row is missing, the role-check policies (once written) will silently deny all access rather than defaulting to `'client'`. New users could find the app completely broken.
- **Location:** No `auth.users` trigger or edge function for post-registration role assignment was found in the provided code

---

### 🔵 LOW

---

**GAP-13 — No email or in-app notification for any event**
- **Severity:** Low
- **Risk:** The studio receives no alert when a new booking is confirmed, a new message arrives, or a file is uploaded. Admin must manually check Supabase or Stripe to know anything happened.
- **Location:** `supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts` — webhook records the booking but sends no notification; no email service is configured anywhere in the provided code

---

**GAP-14 — No file deletion policy**
- **Severity:** Low
- **Risk:** Clients and staff cannot delete files once uploaded. In a HIPAA context, clients have a right to request deletion of their health records. With no delete policy, this cannot be honoured without manual Supabase dashboard access.
- **Location:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — no `DELETE` policy on `storage.objects` for `client-files`

---

**GAP-15 — No message deletion or editing**
- **Severity:** Low
- **Risk:** If a client sends a message containing sensitive information they meant to withhold, neither party can retract it. There is no soft-delete or edit capability.
- **Location:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — no `UPDATE` or `DELETE` policy on `messages`

---

**GAP-16 — CORS configuration for edge functions is not visible**
- **Severity:** Low
- **Risk:** Without explicit CORS headers (rules that control which websites are allowed to call your server), the edge functions may either reject legitimate browser calls or — if Supabase's default is permissive — accept calls from any website on the internet.
- **Location:** `supabase/functions/checkout/index.ts` and `supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts` — neither returns `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` headers or handles preflight `OPTIONS` requests

---

**GAP-17 — Booking status vocabulary is an unconstrained text field**
- **Severity:** Low
- **Risk:** `bookings.status` has no `CHECK` constraint. Only `'paid'` is ever written (by the webhook), but future code could accidentally write `'Paid'`, `'complete'`, or any other string, causing silent query mismatches.
- **Location:** `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` — `status text` with no `CHECK (status IN ('paid', 'cancelled', 'refunded', ...))`

---

*End of Gap List.*
